exercise.goal: Categorize traditional items by their symbolic roles in honoring ancestors.

questions.answer: Guiding Lights: Item 1 (Copal incense), Item 3 (Candles), Item 6 (Cempasuchil petals). Memory Items: Item 2 (Sugar skull), Item 4 (Framed photo), Item 5 (Pan de muerto).
questions.prompt: Examine the six item cards above. Classify each numbered item into one of two categories: 'Guiding Lights' (items used to light or scent the path for spirits) or 'Memory Items' (items representing personal remembrance, food, or offerings). Write your sorted items clearly.

questions.answer: Result is 5. Explanation should state why the chosen item honors ancestors.
questions.prompt: Choose either the Cempasuchil flower or the framed photograph. Write a short explanation (2-3 sentences) detailing why this specific item plays an important role in honoring family ancestors during Dia de los Muertos.

stimuli.label: Card 1
stimuli.text: Item 1: Copal incense burned in clay copaleros to purify the air and create a fragrant pathway for returning souls.

stimuli.label: Card 2
stimuli.text: Item 2: Decorated sugar skulls representing the sweetness of life and honoring the memory of departed individuals.

stimuli.label: Card 3
stimuli.text: Item 3: Beeswax candles placed on the altar to provide a flickering flame that guides spirits back to their homes.

stimuli.label: Card 4
stimuli.text: Item 4: Framed photographs placed prominently on the altar to center remembrance on specific family ancestors.

stimuli.label: Card 5
stimuli.text: Item 5: Sweet, traditional pan de muerto bread baked as a nourishing food offering for the traveling souls.

stimuli.label: Card 6
stimuli.text: Item 6: Bright orange cempasuchil (marigold) flower petals scattered to create vibrant trails for visiting spirits.
